rounds.proof_sketch: With shape [128, 4000] and dim=1: outer_size=128, dim_size=4000, inner_size=1. Block is dim3(1), so only one thread per block. For any 1D block with size 1, threadIdx.x = threadIdx.z = 0. The mutation has no effect.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes threadIdx.x to threadIdx.z, but this only causes behavioral differences when inner_size > 1 (multiple threads per block). With the fixed input shape [128, 4000] and fixed dim=1, inner_size computes to 1. A dim3 block of size 1 has threadIdx components all equal to 0, making threadIdx.x and threadIdx.z interchangeable. The 112 rounds of bitwise-identical testing confirm this analysis. No input value can change inner_size since it depends solely on tensor shape and the fixed dim parameter.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed configuration. The mutation would only be distinguishable if dim=0 (giving inner_size=4000), but dim is part of model configuration, not variable input values. With dim=1, inner_size=1, making threadIdx.x ≡ threadIdx.z ≡ 0.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for CUDA kernels should consider thread indexing mutations as configuration-dependent. A kernel that appears equivalent under one dimension parameter may be catastrophically broken under another. Test coverage should include multiple dimension parameters when testing cumprod-style operations that compute different thread counts based on dim.
